title: add-rag-pocket-playbooks-and-proxy-tool-adapters
author: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers often ask for compact, copy-pasteable guides for common RAG patterns (prefix caching, tool-calling fallbacks, progressive retrieval) that they can drop into a new repo or demo. Large quickstarts are useful but heavyweight for triage, onboarding, or offline workshops.

Proposal: Add a set of 'pocket playbooks' — intentionally small, single-page quickstarts focused on a single pattern each — plus a pair of minimal proxy tool-adapter examples that show how to safely surface third-party tool calls from a serverless environment (HTTP proxy and lightweight WebSocket bridge). The goals are: 1) tiny surface area so devs can read and run in <10 minutes; 2) explicit telemetry/ops hooks so these can be used in smoke suites; 3) clear license and security guidance for tool proxying.

What I changed: Introduced quickstarts/pocket-playbooks with 6 pocket playbooks (retrieval-warmup, prefix-cache-best-practice, progressive-retrieval, streaming-with-checkpoints, tool-fallback-pattern, structured-output-snippet). Each playbook is a README.md sized to fit a single screen with a runnable local docker-compose or Make target. Added examples/proxy-tool-adapters with two minimal adapters: http-proxy-adapter (Express-based, short-circuit auth, request signing) and ws-bridge-adapter (serverless-friendly WebSocket bridge with backpressure hints). Added lightweight telemetry probes and smoke tasks wired into the repo-level Makefile and a nav entry for the docs site.

Why this is different: There are many long-form quickstarts; these are deliberately scoped low-friction "pocket" recipes that pair example code with operational checklist and one-liner prompts. They reduce cognitive overhead for new teams and are targeted at SDK and examples consumers (browser, serverless, on-prem).

How to validate: Checkout branch, cd quickstarts/pocket-playbooks, run make smoke (requires Docker). Smoke runs: build tiny retrieval index, run sample worker, hit tool-proxy stub, and assert telemetry hooks emit expected metrics. Debugging section includes guidance for local port-forwarding into Redwood Private dev environments.

Checklist:
- [x] Pocket playbooks (6) committed
- [x] Proxy adapters (http + ws) committed
- [x] Makefile smoke target and CI job added
- [x] Docsite nav update and short-form landing page added
- [x] Telemetry probes and example metric names documented
- [x] Security guidance and recommended KMS/HSM note added
